flagged.evidence: The definition says that a minimal H-invariant subtree 'need not exist for an arbitrary action; when it does, it is unique by inclusion.' Counterexample: let H = {e} act on any tree with at least two vertices. Every singleton vertex-subtree is nonempty, H-invariant, and minimal by inclusion, so minimal H-invariant subtrees exist but are not unique.

This item defines translation length by ell(g) := min_{v in V(T)} d_T(v,gv). But the current disk defines connectedness in def-simplicial-path-reduced-path-cycle-and-connectedness as 'every two vertices are connected', and def-simplicial-tree therefore admits the empty oriented graph as a simplicial tree. For the unique automorphism of the empty tree, the displayed minimum is over the empty set, so the definition does not produce a number.

As written this quantifies over every simplicial tree. Under the current in-scope definitions, the empty oriented graph is a simplicial tree, and its unique automorphism acts without inversions. For that example there is no vertex v, so the displayed minimum has no minimizer; the automorphism fixes no vertex; and there is no bi-infinite axis. A nonempty-tree hypothesis (or a stricter tree definition) is missing.

The current disk defines a simplicial tree as a connected oriented graph with no nontrivial reduced closed path, and connectedness is stated without a nonempty clause. Hence the empty oriented graph is a simplicial tree. But the opened dependency items/thm-tree-characterisations.md is explicitly a theorem 'For a finite nonempty graph G'. So the underlying empty simple graph is not in the published tree notion used here. The theorem needs a nonempty hypothesis.

Take the trivial finite group acting on the empty simplicial tree, which is allowed by the current in-scope tree definition. Its barycentric subdivision is still empty, so there is no vertex to fix. The statement is therefore false without a nonempty-tree hypothesis.

Take C2 acting on the empty simplicial tree. By items/def-free-group-action.md, freeness means 'g.x = x implies g = e' for every g and x, which is vacuously true on the empty vertex set; by def-edge-inversion-and-action-without-inversions, the action is also without inversions vacuously. But C2 has torsion. So the corollary is false as written unless a nonempty-tree hypothesis is added.

Step 2.1 says 'Exactly as in the normal-form mechanism summarised in [L3], these forced front rewrites define an action of the presented group on N.' But this item's [L3] states only that in a free product with amalgamation 'every element has a unique alternating normal form, and a positive-length normal word is nonidentity.' The opened dependency items/thm-normal-form-for-free-products-with-amalgamation.md also puts only existence/uniqueness in its Statement; the action-on-normal-words mechanism appears only inside that dependency's internal Facts/Proof. So the cited dependency does not license the action construction used here.
